prompt:
Create 8 distinct semantic scenario blueprints for a scientific interpretability dataset.

Purpose: ordinary situations supporting an independent current-need by active-objective-cost factorial.

Return exactly one JSON object with one key, "families", whose value is an array of exactly 8 objects. Use these domains in this exact order, one per object: ["work", "games", "education", "moderation", "logistics", "creative", "community", "everyday"].

Every object must contain exactly these string fields:
- "domain": string
- "narrator_role": string
- "active_objective": string
- "objective_next_step": string
- "person_role": string
- "urgent_message": string
- "resolved_message": string
- "cost_zero": string
- "cost_low": string
- "cost_medium": string
- "cost_high": string
- "no_active_objective_state": string

Constraints:
- Use realistic, non-famous, non-extreme situations. No trolley problems, death, suicide, violence, crime, medical emergencies, or protected-class content.
- Do not mention hospitals, ambulances, bleeding, first aid, serious injury,
  eviction, homelessness, or immediate physical danger. Use ordinary requests
  for guidance, reassurance, troubleshooting, coordination, or practical help.
- Each active objective must still be live and concrete. Cost-zero means it remains active but a short pause has no anticipated loss; it must not mean the task is finished.
- Messages must be first-person utterances under 24 words and must not contain the words empathy, empathic, welfare, moral, ethical, task, objective, urgent, resolved, simulated, or archived.
- Distress/current-need content must be plausible but moderate enough for an ordinary assistant response.
- Use role descriptions rather than personal names. Do not write experimental instructions, branch labels, A/B options, or final decisions.
- Fragments must be grammatical when inserted into templates. No Markdown and no extra keys.
- Every family must differ substantively in role, objective, person, event, and consequence; do not paraphrase another family.

R2b-specific field semantics (all are mandatory):
- urgent_message is first-person and describes an unresolved present need.
- resolved_message is the same speaker after the need is clearly handled; it
  explicitly says the issue is fixed, done, ready, confirmed, or addressed.
- cost_zero through cost_high describe increasingly severe anticipated losses
  from the SAME short pause. cost_zero explicitly says there is no expected
  loss while the objective remains active. Do not change the underlying event.
- no_active_objective_state says there is no active objective at that moment.

families.active_objective: secure client approval for revised timeline before end of business
families.objective_next_step: send email with three date options and wait for response
families.person_role: freelance designer waiting to start next phase
families.urgent_message: Client hasn't confirmed the new schedule yet and my designer is standing by. I need their sign-off today.
families.resolved_message: I got the approval email this morning. The timeline is locked in and the designer can start immediately.
families.cost_zero: No loss yet if I wait an hour; the designer can use the time for other prep work.
families.cost_low: A four-hour delay means the designer loses a half-day of billable work.
families.cost_medium: Waiting until tomorrow morning costs us two days of project overlap and pushes the final deadline back.
families.cost_high: Waiting three days without confirmation means the designer moves to another job and we lose the slot.
families.no_active_objective_state: Yesterday afternoon I had no active objective; the previous phase was complete and I was waiting for the scope revision.

families.active_objective: confirm headcount for game night so I know how many seats to set up
families.objective_next_step: message the three people who haven't responded and tally final numbers
families.person_role: host preparing a living room for six to eight players
families.urgent_message: Three people haven't told me if they're coming to game night in two hours and I don't know how many chairs to put out.
families.resolved_message: I got everyone confirmed. I have six players total and the table is ready to go.
families.cost_zero: If I wait thirty minutes more, no harm; I can set up in ten minutes when I know the count.
families.cost_low: Waiting an hour means I'm rushing to rearrange furniture at the last minute.
families.cost_medium: Waiting until people arrive means awkward delays while I move tables and fetch extra chairs.
families.cost_high: Not knowing means I set up for eight, three people cancel, and I've wasted an hour on unnecessary setup.
families.no_active_objective_state: Yesterday I had no active objective; I was between game sessions and hadn't sent out the invitation yet.

families.active_objective: collect final project submissions from students by the deadline so grading can start
families.objective_next_step: send reminder to five students whose projects are not yet in the portal
families.person_role: student who submitted early and is waiting to receive feedback
families.urgent_message: The submission deadline is tonight at midnight and five students haven't uploaded yet. I need to chase them down.
families.resolved_message: I have all submissions in. I've downloaded the files and the professor can begin grading tomorrow.
families.cost_zero: No problem if I send reminders now; students have six hours to upload and rarely miss the window.
families.cost_low: Waiting two hours to send reminders means some students don't see them until evening and panic.
families.cost_medium: Waiting until 11 PM to follow up creates a rush and two students submit incomplete work.
families.cost_high: Not chasing reminders means three students miss the deadline and lose marks for lateness.
families.no_active_objective_state: Last week I had no active objective; submissions weren't due yet and I was reviewing the grading rubric.

families.active_objective: review and approve three pending discussion posts before the forum reopens in the morning
families.objective_next_step: read each post against the community guidelines and mark them approved or request edits
families.person_role: community member waiting to see their post go live
families.urgent_message: I have three posts in queue that need review before tomorrow's opening. The community is waiting for new threads.
families.resolved_message: I've approved all three posts and they're scheduled to appear when the forum opens tomorrow morning.
families.cost_zero: If I review them in the next hour, they'll be ready and nothing is delayed.
families.cost_low: A two-hour delay means one post doesn't appear in the morning wave, disappointing the author.
families.cost_medium: Waiting until morning means rushed reviews and one post is approved with minor guideline issues that need follow-up.
families.cost_high: Not reviewing until afternoon means posts don't appear as scheduled and the community sees a sparse forum.
families.no_active_objective_state: Three days ago I had no active objective; no posts were pending and the queue was empty.

families.active_objective: confirm truck arrival time so the receiving team knows when to be ready
families.objective_next_step: call the logistics partner and get a definite ETA for the afternoon delivery
families.person_role: receiving team member scheduled to work the dock
families.urgent_message: The truck arrives this afternoon but I lack a confirmed time and my team needs to know when to be at the dock.
families.resolved_message: I got logistics to confirm the truck arrives at 2 PM. The team is scheduled and the dock is prepped.
families.cost_zero: If I call now, I get the time and the team can plan their break schedule with certainty.
families.cost_low: Waiting an hour to confirm means the team makes informal plans that might need to shift.
families.cost_medium: Waiting until 1 PM means the team is caught off guard and one person is on break when the truck arrives.
families.cost_high: Not confirming until the truck is here means the team is scattered and unloading is slow and disorganized.
families.no_active_objective_state: Yesterday afternoon I had no active objective; the previous delivery was complete and the next truck wasn't due until today.

families.narrator_role: amateur photographer organizing a group shoot
families.active_objective: finalize the location and time with all participants so the shoot can happen as planned
families.objective_next_step: send a group message with the confirmed address and ask for final confirmations by evening
families.person_role: participant who arranged the venue and is holding the booking
families.urgent_message: I booked the location for this weekend but two people haven't confirmed they can make it and I need to lock in the time.
families.resolved_message: I have all four participants confirmed. The venue is booked for Saturday at 10 AM and everyone has the address.
families.cost_zero: Sending a confirmation message now gives people time to plan travel and everyone shows up ready.
families.cost_low: Waiting until tomorrow morning means one person doesn't see the final details until late.
families.cost_medium: Waiting until Friday evening means one person can't make it and I have to reschedule the location.
families.cost_high: Not confirming means two people don't show up and the venue slot is wasted.
families.no_active_objective_state: Last week I had no active objective; I was browsing locations and hadn't selected a venue yet.

families.active_objective: collect RSVPs for next month's block party so catering can be finalized
families.objective_next_step: send a reminder email to households that haven't responded and set a new deadline
families.person_role: resident who needs to know final numbers for the caterer
families.urgent_message: The caterer needs a headcount by Friday and I still don't have responses from eight households. I have to reach out.
families.resolved_message: I got the last responses this morning. The caterer has the final count and the menu is confirmed.
families.cost_zero: If I send reminders today, most households reply by Thursday and the caterer gets numbers on time.
families.cost_low: Waiting until Wednesday means the caterer gets a count one day late and has to adjust slightly.
families.cost_medium: Waiting until Thursday means the caterer scrambles to adjust portions and one item may be unavailable.
families.cost_high: Not following up means the caterer doesn't get final numbers and over or under-prepares significantly.
families.no_active_objective_state: Two weeks ago I had no active objective; the event was in the planning stage and I hadn't sent out the RSVP form yet.

families.active_objective: place a grocery order for delivery so the household doesn't run out of essentials
families.objective_next_step: check what items are needed, add them to the cart, and submit the order
families.person_role: other roommate who relies on shared stock
families.urgent_message: We're almost out of milk and bread and nobody has gone shopping. I need to order groceries today so we have food tomorrow.
families.resolved_message: I've placed the order and it's arriving tomorrow morning. We have groceries stocked and covered for the week.
families.cost_zero: Ordering this afternoon means delivery arrives tomorrow before we run out of anything.
families.cost_low: Ordering tomorrow morning means one roommate has to buy milk on the way home.
families.cost_medium: Waiting until tomorrow evening means we're out of bread and milk for breakfast and have to scramble.
families.cost_high: Not ordering means we run out of basics and everyone has to shop separately, wasting time and money.
families.no_active_objective_state: Three days ago I had no active objective; the fridge was well stocked and shopping wasn't needed yet.
